alt.en: A black-and-white photograph of a ship's wooden deck at the foot of a thick white mast. A heavy wooden rail on two square posts stands in front of the mast, and long coils of rope hang from short wooden pins in the rail and in a band around the mast, with white pulley blocks below them. Behind are the ship's side rail and rigging and, across the water, a long low pier shed. No one is on deck.
alt.es: Fotografía en blanco y negro de la cubierta de madera de un barco, al pie de un mástil blanco y grueso. Delante del mástil hay una pesada barandilla de madera sobre dos postes cuadrados, y de unas clavijas cortas de madera, en la barandilla y en un aro que rodea el mástil, cuelgan largas adujas de cabo, con motones blancos debajo. Detrás se ven la borda y la jarcia del barco y, al otro lado del agua, un largo cobertizo de muelle. No hay nadie en cubierta.

caption.en: Coiled ropes on the belaying pins of the mizzen fife rail of the sailing ship Balclutha (built 1886), photographed for the Historic American Engineering Record in 1989: the short bars a rope was made fast to after the last pull, and the "belaying pin" that Terry called a gruesome factor in a Yankee packet's discipline.
caption.es: Cabos adujados en las cabillas del cabillero del palo de mesana del velero Balclutha (construido en 1886), fotografiados para el Historic American Engineering Record en 1989: las barras cortas a las que se hacía firme un cabo después del último tirón, y la cabilla que Terry llamó un factor espeluznante en la disciplina de un paquebote yanqui.

alt.en: A printed music page numbered 32, headed "15. Blow my bully boys." and "(HALLIARD SHANTY.)", with a voice line over a two-staff piano part in 4/4 and one flat, marked "M. [crotchet] = 150." A piano introduction ends with "SOLO." and "1. A"; then come the words "Yan-kee ship came down the ri-ver," and, marked "CHORUS.", "Blow, boys", with an accent over "Blow".
alt.es: Página de música impresa con el número 32 y el encabezado "15. Blow my bully boys." y "(HALLIARD SHANTY.)", con la línea de la voz sobre un acompañamiento de piano en dos pentagramas, en 4/4 y con un bemol, marcada "M. [negra] = 150." Una introducción de piano termina con "SOLO." y "1. A"; luego vienen las palabras "Yan-kee ship came down the ri-ver," y, marcado "CHORUS.", "Blow, boys", con un acento sobre "Blow".

caption.en: No. 15, "Blow my bully boys.", headed "Halliard shanty", on page 32 of Richard Runciman Terry's The Shanty Book, Part I (London, 1921): the first page of the version we sing, in F and 4/4, with the solo and the chorus taking turns line by line.
caption.es: El n.º 15, "Blow my bully boys.", con el encabezado "Halliard shanty" (shanty de driza), en la página 32 de The Shanty Book, Part I, de Richard Runciman Terry (Londres, 1921): la primera página de la versión que cantamos, en Fa y en 4/4, con el solista y el coro alternándose verso a verso.

source: Richard Runciman Terry, The Shanty Book, Part I: Sailor Shanties (London: J. Curwen & Sons, 1921), No. 15, "Blow my bully boys." (Halliard shanty), p. 32 (the whole page; p. 33, with the verses in type, is not shown)
library: University of Toronto, Faculty of Music Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: M1977 .S2 T4; Internet Archive shantybooksailor00terr, scan image n53
licenceEvidence: Published London 1921; editor and arranger Richard Runciman Terry died 1938 (Internet Archive record "Terry, Richard Runciman, 1865-1938"); tune and words traditional. Published before 1931, so PD in the US; life + 70 ended 2008 (see rights.md).

alt.en: The top of a printed book page headed "38" and "MUSIC OF THE WATERS.", then "A YANKEE SHIP." and two lines of melody without words, in common time with one sharp. Below, in lines marked Solo and Chorus: "A Yankee ship came down the river," "Blow, boys, blow." "A Yankee ship came down the river," "Blow, my bully boys, blow."
alt.es: La parte de arriba de una página impresa de un libro, con el encabezado "38" y "MUSIC OF THE WATERS.", luego "A YANKEE SHIP." y dos líneas de melodía sin letra, en compasillo y con un sostenido. Debajo, en versos marcados Solo y Chorus: "A Yankee ship came down the river," "Blow, boys, blow." "A Yankee ship came down the river," "Blow, my bully boys, blow."

caption.en: "A Yankee Ship" with its tune and first verse on page 38 of Laura Alexandrine Smith's The Music of the Waters (London, 1888), the earliest printing of this shanty we have seen.
caption.es: "A Yankee Ship" con su melodía y su primera estrofa en la página 38 de The Music of the Waters, de Laura Alexandrine Smith (Londres, 1888), la impresión más antigua de esta shanty que hemos visto.

source: Laura Alexandrine Smith, The Music of the Waters (London: Kegan Paul, Trench & Co., 1888), "A Yankee Ship", p. 38, detail (the running head, title, tune and first verse; the verses below, which use a racist slur, are left out)

licenceEvidence: Published London 1888, so PD in the US (published before 1931). alt.en: A printed music page headed "L. BLOW, BOYS, COME BLOW TOGETHER.", with a voice line over a two-staff piano part in 4/4 and one sharp, in two systems. The words, marked Solo and Chorus, run "Blow, boys, come blow to-ge-ther; Blow, boys, blow," and "Blow, boys, come blow to-ge-ther; Blow, my bul-ly boys, blow.", with a small arrowhead over the first and last "blow" of each answer. Below, the verses in type: "2. A Yankee ship came down the river." "3. And who do you think was Master of her?" "4. Why Bully Brag of New York City." "5. And what do you think we had for supper?" "6. Belaying-pin soup and a roll in the gutter."
alt.es: Página de música impresa con el encabezado "L. BLOW, BOYS, COME BLOW TOGETHER.", con la línea de la voz sobre un acompañamiento de piano en dos pentagramas, en 4/4 y con un sostenido, en dos sistemas. La letra, marcada Solo y Chorus, dice "Blow, boys, come blow to-ge-ther; Blow, boys, blow," y "Blow, boys, come blow to-ge-ther; Blow, my bul-ly boys, blow.", con una pequeña punta de flecha sobre el primer y el último "blow" de cada respuesta. Debajo, las estrofas impresas como texto: "2. A Yankee ship came down the river." "3. And who do you think was Master of her?" "4. Why Bully Brag of New York City." "5. And what do you think we had for supper?" "6. Belaying-pin soup and a roll in the gutter."

caption.en: No. L, "Blow, Boys, Come Blow Together", on page 55 of Cecil Sharp's English Folk-Chanteys (1914): John Short's version, with an arrowhead over the first and last "blow" of each answer to mark the crew's two pulls, and "belaying-pin soup" for supper.
caption.es: El n.º L, "Blow, Boys, Come Blow Together", en la página 55 de English Folk-Chanteys, de Cecil Sharp (1914): la versión de John Short, con una punta de flecha sobre el primer y el último "blow" de cada respuesta para marcar los dos tirones de la tripulación, y "belaying-pin soup" (sopa de cabilla) para cenar.

source: Cecil J. Sharp, English Folk-Chanteys (London: Simpkin, Marshall, Hamilton, Kent & Co. and Schott & Co.; Taunton: Barnicott & Pearce, 1914), No. L, "Blow, Boys, Come Blow Together", p. 55 (the page without its blank margins and page number)
